destinations.name: Gokak Falls
destinations.highlights: 170 ft Ghataprabha plunge · Historic 201 m hanging bridge
destinations.description: Known as the "Niagara of Karnataka," Gokak Falls cascades 170 ft over stratified red sandstone cliffs on the Ghataprabha River, spanned by a century-old suspension footbridge.
destinations.imageAlt: Gokak Falls cascading over sandstone cliffs beneath a historic suspension bridge

destinations.name: Belagavi Fort & Kamal Basti
destinations.highlights: 12th-century Ratta fortification · Carved lotus stone dome
destinations.description: Built in 1204 CE by the Ratta dynasty, this oval stone citadel houses the exquisite Kamal Basadi Jain temple featuring a multi-tiered carved black basalt lotus dome and lathe-turned pillars.
destinations.imageAlt: Ancient stone ramparts of Belagavi Fort and the Kamal Basadi Chalukyan Jain temple

destinations.name: Rajhansgad (Yellur Fort)
destinations.highlights: 360° Sahyadri valley views · Hilltop Siddheshwar temple
destinations.description: Perched atop an emerald ridge near Yellur village, Rajhansgad offers sweeping panoramic views of terraced farmland, ancient stone ramparts, a freshwater well, and a serene hilltop Shiva shrine.
destinations.imageAlt: Hilltop stone fort ramparts at Rajhansgad overlooking misty green Belagavi valleys

destinations.name: Kittur Rani Channamma Fort & Palace
destinations.description: Historic seat of Queen Rani Channamma, revered symbol of India’s earliest armed resistance against colonial rule, featuring arched stone gateways, palace foundations, and a state museum.
destinations.imageAlt: Stone arched gateway and landscaped ruins of Kittur Rani Channamma Fort

destinations.name: Godchinamalaki Falls
destinations.highlights: Two-tier Markandeya cascade · Rugged forest gorge trek
destinations.description: Tucked inside a deep green canyon along the Markandeya River near Gokak, this picturesque two-tier waterfall rewards visitors with mossy boulder trails and quiet forest views.
destinations.imageAlt: Two-tier Godchinamalaki waterfall surrounded by lush green valley trees

destinations.name: Bhimgad Wildlife Sanctuary
destinations.highlights: Western Ghats biodiversity · Barapede limestone caves
destinations.description: Located in the lush Khanapur Western Ghats, Bhimgad protects dense tropical evergreen forests, Mahadayi river headwaters, misty ridge trails, and rare limestone caves.
destinations.imageAlt: Misty tropical rainforest trail inside Bhimgad Wildlife Sanctuary, Khanapur

food.title: Belagavi Kunda
food.description: Belagavi’s signature caramelized milk delicacy slow-simmered for hours in heavy iron kadhais with khoya, caramelized sugar, and fragrant green cardamom.
food.imageAlt: Caramelized Belagavi Kunda milk fudge garnished with pistachios in a brass bowl

food.title: Gokak Karadant
food.description: Wholesome heritage fudge crafted from edible gum (ant), organic jaggery, roasted almonds, cashews, pistachios, and dry coconut—prized for warmth and stamina.
food.imageAlt: Nut-rich Gokak Karadant squares arranged on a traditional brass platter

food.title: Jolada Roti & Enne Gai
food.description: Hand-patted crisp sorghum flatbreads paired with spiced sesame-peanut stuffed brinjal curry (Enne Gai), roasted groundnut chutney pudi, fresh curd, and raw onion.
food.imageAlt: Traditional North Karnataka Jolada Rotti thali with Enne Gai brinjal curry

food.title: Belagavi Biryani & Mandige
food.description: Fragrant regional dum biryani infused with Malnad spices served alongside paper-thin, melt-in-the-mouth sweet Mandige flatbread dusted with sugar and nutmeg.
food.imageAlt: Aromatic Belagavi spiced biryani in a copper handi alongside sweet folded Mandige

art.title: Gokak Wooden Toys
art.description: Turned from lightweight local wood and finished with glossy natural vegetable lacquer, these vibrant handcrafted fruits, animals, and folk figurines date back two centuries.
art.imageAlt: Colorful lacquered Gokak wooden toys and fruit replicas on an artisan bench

art.title: Khanapur Terracotta & Pottery
art.description: Hand-thrown water matkas, slow-cooking handis, and architectural terracotta tiles shaped from mineral-rich Malaprabha clay and fired in traditional open kilns.
art.imageAlt: Rows of hand-thrown red terracotta clay pots drying in a Khanapur courtyard

art.title: Shahapur Handloom & Ilkal Sarees
art.description: Generations of weavers in Belagavi’s Shahapur quarter craft breathable cotton-silk sarees featuring crisp geometric checks, temple borders, and Kasuti-inspired motifs.
art.imageAlt: Traditional handloom Ilkal and Shahapur sarees with woven borders on a wooden loom

art.title: Chalukyan & Ratta Stone Sculpture
art.description: Intricate multi-petaled lotus domes, mythological friezes, and mirror-polished lathe-turned basalt columns showcasing 12th-century Kalyana Chalukya craftsmanship.
art.imageAlt: Carved black basalt lotus ceiling and stone pillars inside Kamal Basti Belagavi

culture.title: Kittur Utsava
culture.description: An annual three-day celebration honoring Rani Channamma’s 1824 victory with illuminated fort processions, traditional wrestling, Janapada folk theatre, and equestrian parades.
culture.imageAlt: Illuminated Kittur Utsava cultural procession at the stone fort gate at dusk

culture.title: Belagavi Kite Festival
culture.description: Held every Makar Sankranti season, Belagavi’s breezy winter skies fill with hundreds of artistic kites flown by teams across India alongside folk music and regional food stalls.
culture.imageAlt: Colorful kites soaring over rolling green meadows during the Belagavi Kite Festival

culture.title: Ganesh Chaturthi & Navaratri
culture.description: Belagavi’s bilingual heritage shines through grand sarvajanik mandaps, glowing brass deepam lamps, classical bhajan recitals, and artistic tableaux uniting Kannada and Marathi customs.
culture.imageAlt: Warmly lit brass lamps and marigold garlands during Ganesh Chaturthi in Belagavi

culture.title: Dollu Kunitha & Folk Performances
culture.description: Accompanied by thunderous cylindrical drums and rhythmic footwork, Dollu Kunitha troupes bring vibrant choreography and oral ballads to regional temple fairs and cultural nights.
culture.imageAlt: Traditional Dollu Kunitha folk drummers performing in crimson attire at golden hour
